cases.prompt: Fix the off-by-one sum so the upper bound is included and zero remains valid.
cases.source: pub fn sum(upper: u32) -> u64 { (1..upper).map(u64::from).sum() }
cases.reference: pub fn sum(upper: u32) -> u64 { (1..=upper).map(u64::from).sum() }
cases.tests: #[test] fn upper_bound() { assert_eq!(sum(0), 0); assert_eq!(sum(1), 1); assert_eq!(sum(4), 10); }

cases.prompt: Return None for an empty input rather than inventing a value.
cases.source: pub fn first(values: &[i32]) -> Option<i32> { values.first().copied().or(Some(0)) }
cases.reference: pub fn first(values: &[i32]) -> Option<i32> { values.first().copied() }
cases.tests: #[test] fn empty_input() { assert_eq!(first(&[]), None); assert_eq!(first(&[7, 8]), Some(7)); }

cases.prompt: Slice by Unicode scalar values without corrupting UTF-8 or panicking.
cases.source: pub fn prefix(text: &str, count: usize) -> String { String::from_utf8_lossy(&text.as_bytes()[..count.min(text.len())]).into_owned() }
cases.reference: pub fn prefix(text: &str, count: usize) -> String { text.chars().take(count).collect() }
cases.tests: #[test] fn unicode_prefix() { assert_eq!(prefix("a\u{e9}z", 2), "a\u{e9}"); assert_eq!(prefix("", 2), ""); assert_eq!(prefix("abc", 10), "abc"); }

cases.prompt: Report integer overflow instead of wrapping it.
cases.source: pub fn add(left: u32, right: u32) -> Option<u32> { Some(left.wrapping_add(right)) }
cases.reference: pub fn add(left: u32, right: u32) -> Option<u32> { left.checked_add(right) }
cases.tests: #[test] fn overflow() { assert_eq!(add(2, 3), Some(5)); assert_eq!(add(u32::MAX, 1), None); }

cases.prompt: Sort by the first tuple field while preserving original order for equal keys.
cases.source: pub fn ordered(mut items: Vec<(u32, u32)>) -> Vec<(u32, u32)> { items.sort_by_key(|&(key, identity)| (key, std::cmp::Reverse(identity))); items }
cases.reference: pub fn ordered(mut items: Vec<(u32, u32)>) -> Vec<(u32, u32)> { items.sort_by_key(|&(key, _identity)| key); items }
cases.tests: #[test] fn stable_order() { assert_eq!(ordered(vec![(1, 1), (1, 2), (0, 3)]), vec![(0, 3), (1, 1), (1, 2)]); }

cases.prompt: Deduplicate without changing first-occurrence order.
cases.source: pub fn unique(mut values: Vec<u32>) -> Vec<u32> { values.sort(); values.dedup(); values }
cases.reference: pub fn unique(values: Vec<u32>) -> Vec<u32> { let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new(); values.into_iter().filter(|value| seen.insert(*value)).collect() }
cases.tests: #[test] fn first_occurrences() { assert_eq!(unique(vec![3, 1, 3, 2, 1]), vec![3, 1, 2]); assert!(unique(vec![]).is_empty()); }

cases.prompt: Apply the Gregorian leap-year rule at century boundaries.
cases.source: pub fn leap(year: u32) -> bool { year % 4 == 0 }
cases.reference: pub fn leap(year: u32) -> bool { year % 4 == 0 && (year % 100 != 0 || year % 400 == 0) }
cases.tests: #[test] fn century_boundary() { assert!(!leap(1900)); assert!(leap(2000)); assert!(leap(2024)); assert!(!leap(2023)); }

cases.prompt: Accept only nonempty normal relative path components; reject traversal and absolute paths.
cases.source: pub fn local(path: &std::path::Path) -> bool { !path.is_absolute() }
cases.reference: pub fn local(path: &std::path::Path) -> bool { !path.as_os_str().is_empty() && path.components().all(|part| matches!(part, std::path::Component::Normal(_))) }
cases.tests: #[test] fn safe_paths() { use std::path::Path; assert!(local(Path::new("src/lib.rs"))); assert!(!local(Path::new("../private"))); assert!(!local(Path::new("/private"))); assert!(!local(Path::new(""))); }

cases.prompt: Validate the required JSON count field and return a stable error for missing or mistyped data.
cases.source: pub fn count(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<u64, &'static str> { Ok(value.get("count").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(0)) }
cases.reference: pub fn count(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<u64, &'static str> { value.get("count").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_u64).ok_or("invalid count") }
cases.tests: #[test] fn required_field() { assert_eq!(count(&serde_json::json!({})), Err("invalid count")); assert_eq!(count(&serde_json::json!({"count": 7})), Ok(7)); assert_eq!(count(&serde_json::json!({"count": "7"})), Err("invalid count")); }

cases.prompt: Preserve escaped JSON string semantics using serde_json, including newline and embedded quotes.
cases.source: pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<String, serde_json::Error> { serde_json::from_str::<String>(text).map(|value| value.replace('\n', "\\n")) }
cases.reference: pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<String, serde_json::Error> { serde_json::from_str::<String>(text) }
cases.tests: #[test] fn escaped_strings() { assert_eq!(parse("\"line\\nquote\\\"\"").unwrap(), "line\nquote\""); assert!(parse("unterminated").is_err()); }

cases.prompt: Propagate parse and overflow errors instead of turning invalid input into success.
cases.source: pub fn double(text: &str) -> Result<u32, &'static str> { Ok(text.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0).wrapping_mul(2)) }
cases.reference: pub fn double(text: &str) -> Result<u32, &'static str> { text.parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| "invalid")?.checked_mul(2).ok_or("overflow") }
cases.tests: #[test] fn error_propagation() { assert_eq!(double("bad"), Err("invalid")); assert_eq!(double("7"), Ok(14)); assert_eq!(double("4294967295"), Err("overflow")); }

cases.prompt: Release the request-local reservation on both normal and cancelled paths.
cases.source: pub fn run(cancelled: bool, live: &std::cell::Cell<u32>) { live.set(live.get() + 1); if cancelled { return; } live.set(live.get() - 1); }
cases.reference: pub fn run(cancelled: bool, live: &std::cell::Cell<u32>) { live.set(live.get() + 1); live.set(live.get() - 1); if cancelled { return; } }
cases.tests: #[test] fn cancellation_cleanup() { let live = std::cell::Cell::new(0); run(true, &live); assert_eq!(live.get(), 0); run(false, &live); assert_eq!(live.get(), 0); }

cases.prompt: Remove the resource leak so the RAII lease is released after the operation.
cases.source: struct Lease<'a>(&'a std::cell::Cell<u32>); impl Drop for Lease<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { self.0.set(self.0.get() - 1); } } pub fn use_resource(live: &std::cell::Cell<u32>) { live.set(live.get() + 1); let lease = Lease(live); std::mem::forget(lease); }
cases.reference: struct Lease<'a>(&'a std::cell::Cell<u32>); impl Drop for Lease<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { self.0.set(self.0.get() - 1); } } pub fn use_resource(live: &std::cell::Cell<u32>) { live.set(live.get() + 1); let _lease = Lease(live); }
cases.tests: #[test] fn resource_release() { let live = std::cell::Cell::new(0); use_resource(&live); assert_eq!(live.get(), 0); use_resource(&live); assert_eq!(live.get(), 0); }

cases.prompt: Preserve FIFO fairness in the request queue.
cases.source: pub fn next(queue: &mut std::collections::VecDeque<u32>) -> Option<u32> { queue.pop_back() }
cases.reference: pub fn next(queue: &mut std::collections::VecDeque<u32>) -> Option<u32> { queue.pop_front() }
cases.tests: #[test] fn fifo() { let mut queue = std::collections::VecDeque::from([1, 2, 3]); assert_eq!(next(&mut queue), Some(1)); assert_eq!(next(&mut queue), Some(2)); assert_eq!(next(&mut queue), Some(3)); assert_eq!(next(&mut queue), None); }

cases.prompt: Treat the limit as total attempts, including zero, and stop after the first success.
cases.source: pub fn retry(limit: u32, mut operation: impl FnMut() -> bool) -> bool { for _attempt in 0..=limit { if operation() { return true; } } false }
cases.reference: pub fn retry(limit: u32, mut operation: impl FnMut() -> bool) -> bool { for _attempt in 0..limit { if operation() { return true; } } false }
cases.tests: #[test] fn attempt_limit() { let mut calls = 0; assert!(!retry(2, || { calls += 1; false })); assert_eq!(calls, 2); assert!(!retry(0, || { calls += 1; true })); assert_eq!(calls, 2); assert!(retry(3, || true)); }

cases.prompt: Map queue-full to 429, queue-timeout to 503 and unknown-model to 404.
cases.source: pub fn status(code: &str) -> u16 { match code { "queue_full" => 503, "queue_timeout" => 429, "model_not_found" => 404, _ => 500 } }
cases.reference: pub fn status(code: &str) -> u16 { match code { "queue_full" => 429, "queue_timeout" => 503, "model_not_found" => 404, _ => 500 } }
cases.tests: #[test] fn http_statuses() { assert_eq!(status("queue_full"), 429); assert_eq!(status("queue_timeout"), 503); assert_eq!(status("model_not_found"), 404); assert_eq!(status("unknown"), 500); }

cases.prompt: Reject malformed or out-of-range CLI context values rather than silently clamping them.
cases.source: pub fn context(text: &str) -> Result<u32, &'static str> { Ok(text.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0).min(16384)) }
cases.reference: pub fn context(text: &str) -> Result<u32, &'static str> { let value = text.parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| "invalid")?; if !(256..=16384).contains(&value) { return Err("range"); } Ok(value) }
cases.tests: #[test] fn cli_limits() { assert_eq!(context("256"), Ok(256)); assert_eq!(context("16384"), Ok(16384)); assert_eq!(context("bad"), Err("invalid")); assert_eq!(context("0"), Err("range")); assert_eq!(context("16385"), Err("range")); }

cases.prompt: Round scaled positive and negative values to the nearest integer rather than truncating.
cases.source: pub fn hundredths(value: f64) -> i64 { (value * 100.0) as i64 }
cases.reference: pub fn hundredths(value: f64) -> i64 { (value * 100.0).round() as i64 }
cases.tests: #[test] fn rounding() { assert_eq!(hundredths(1.236), 124); assert_eq!(hundredths(-1.236), -124); assert_eq!(hundredths(0.0), 0); }

cases.prompt: Use a 30-second timeout only when the configuration is absent; preserve explicit zero and positive values.
cases.source: pub fn timeout(value: Option<u64>) -> u64 { value.unwrap_or(0) }
cases.reference: pub fn timeout(value: Option<u64>) -> u64 { value.unwrap_or(30) }
